extracted.intended_audience: contracting officers, federal procurement officials, government contractors, accounting professionals, and stakeholders involved with Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) and federal procurement rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Notice announcing the Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) Board's recent and upcoming meeting agenda items, statutory duties, and topics for rulemaking and review during early FY2026. Useful for parties tracking CAS harmonization, thresholds, pension treatment, and related rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance of Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) to Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: 41 U.S.C. 1501(c)(2) requires the CAS Board to review and conform CAS, where practicable, to GAAP. The Board will review and discuss public comments received to the proposed rules to eliminate CAS 404, 408, 409, and 411 (90 FR 43994) and issuance of a final rule. The Board will also discuss recently opened cases related to CAS 407, 415 and 416: the three remaining standards that the Board identified in its 2018 Staff Discussion Paper (84 FR 9143) on CAS-GAAP Harmonization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on assessing whether CAS standards can be aligned with GAAP; includes consideration of public comments on proposed eliminations and ongoing cases for remaining standards. The Board has accelerated work on conformance consistent with administration priorities on deregulation and reducing transaction costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory CAS Thresholds and application of CAS to Indefinite Delivery Contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will discuss proposed rulemaking to increase the current regulatory threshold for full CAS coverage, which is $50 million (48 CFR 9903.201-2), and the threshold for disclosure requirements, which is $50 million (48 CFR 9903.202-1), and to address the application of CAS to indefinite delivery contracts considering public comments received from the Staff Discussion Paper (85 FR 51491).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative focus on whether monetary thresholds for full CAS coverage and disclosure should be raised and how CAS should apply to indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract structures; commenters should address policy, compliance burden, and practical impacts on contracting parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost impact of accounting changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will continue discussions on the current handling of cost impact in Part 30 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), including the need for additional clarity of the meaning of increased costs in the aggregate, as that language is used in 41 U.S.C 1503(b), and the handling of cost impacts for unilateral cost accounting practice changes. The Board expects coverage on cost impact of accounting changes to be removed from the FAR by rulemaking and addressed in CAS through rulemaking by the CAS Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key issues include clarifying 'increased costs in the aggregate,' treatment of unilateral practice changes, and transitioning responsibility from FAR to CAS. Stakeholders should provide evidence and analysis on cost measurement, incidence, and administrative implications of any change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pension Harmonization for Extraordinary Events (CAS 412 and CAS 413)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CAS Board will discuss an ANPRM to modify CAS 412 and CAS 413. The ANPRM would be a follow-on to rulemaking issued in 2011 required by the Pension Protection Act (PPA) of 2006. The purpose of the ANPRM is to reconcile the application of the PPA and the CAS adjustment of pension costs for extraordinary events (i.e., curtailment of pension plan benefits, termination of plans, and the accounting of pension plan assets or liabilities following the sale or closing of a corporate segment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on aligning statutory pension rules (PPA) with CAS adjustments for extraordinary events; expected to solicit technical comments on accounting treatment, definitions of extraordinary events, and implementation mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Court and Board Decisions Related to CAS
rubrics_metrics.description: 41 U.S.C 1501(c)(3) requires the CAS Board to annually review disputes brought before the Boards of Contract Appeals (BCAs) or Federal courts involving its standards and consider whether greater clarity in CAS could avoid such disputes. The CAS Board will discuss decisions by the BCAs and Courts involving its standards since the last review conducted in 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative criterion is whether CAS language or application can be clarified to reduce litigation and appeals; reviewers should analyze recent decisions to identify ambiguity, implementation issues, or unintended consequences in the standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings closed to the public; comment and inquiry process
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice advises the public of recent and upcoming meetings. The meetings are closed to the public. While CAS Board meetings are closed to the public, the CAS Board welcomes comments and inquiries, which may be directed to the manager using the contact information provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although meetings are closed, stakeholders are expected to participate via submitted comments or inquiries to the designated manager; contact details are provided (John L. McClung) for submissions and questions. Timeliness and proper routing of comments determine consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of CAS Board agendas pursuant to statute
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice is published pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 1501(d), which requires the CAS Board to publish agendas of its meetings in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agendas must be published in the Federal Register to satisfy statutory transparency requirements; parties relying on agendas for legal or administrative action should reference the Federal Register publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on official Federal Register/PDF for legal research
rubrics_metrics.description: The site displays a prototype XML rendition and is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register. Documents posted include a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov. Until ACFR grants official status, the XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For legal research or citation, verify contents against the official printed or govinfo.gov PDF edition; do not rely solely on the prototype XML page for legal notice or judicial purposes.
